policy.relationship: Claude and Codex artifacts are peer implementations of shared agent behavior. Neither side is the canonical source; each side may be edited first.
policy.maintenance: When one side changes, the active agent must update the counterpart in the same session. Hooks remind immediately and block one-sided commits unless the changed artifact is synchronized or this manifest records an explicit artifact-specific status or exemption.

hooks.name: lib-process-output-policy.py
hooks.note: Process-output classifier for agent_guard.policies.secret_leak: denies process argument/environment listings before permissive branches, including decoded Codex nested exec commands. Safe PID/name diagnostics remain available. The shared guard engine (lib/python/agent_guard, classifiers.py) loads this copy in-process for both runtimes; the Codex copy was removed at the 2026-10-01 cutover.

hooks.name: lib-function-body-policy.py
hooks.note: Shell-introspection classifier for agent_guard.policies.secret_leak: denies printing shell function bodies (which/whence -c/type on a function, functions, typeset -f, $functions), including decoded Codex nested exec commands. The shared guard engine (lib/python/agent_guard, classifiers.py) loads this copy in-process for both runtimes; the Codex copy was removed at the 2026-10-01 cutover.

hooks.name: lib-op-policy.py
hooks.note: 1Password broker output-policy classifier for agent_guard.policies.secret_leak and github_write: allows an op-automations/op-desktop invocation only when its stdout cannot carry a credential; unmatched shapes are denied. Tested by tests/test_op_policy.py. The shared guard engine (lib/python/agent_guard, classifiers.py) loads this copy in-process for both runtimes; the Codex copy was removed at the 2026-10-01 cutover.

hooks.name: elpaca-run.sh
hooks.note: Claude Emacs hook utility; Codex routes Emacs events through codex-hook-wrapper directly.

hooks.name: epoch-brief-freshness.sh
hooks.note: paired PostToolUse wrappers around the Epoch helper projects/shared/scripts/brief_freshness_notice.py, which lists a just-read project brief's possibly stale TODOs once per session and brief. Claude registers on Read|Bash, Codex on its shell matcher; both with timeout 40 (the helper's audit times out at 30). The wrappers differ only in their header comment.

hooks.name: fire-and-forget.sh
hooks.note: Claude utility wrapping notify-emacs-* hooks so the CLI doesn't block on emacsclient. The Codex copy was never registered and was removed when the redundant Codex notify-emacs-hook.sh registrations were dropped in favor of codex-hook-wrapper.

hooks.name: lib-codex-hook-json.sh
hooks.note: Codex payload/functions.exec normalizer for the remaining shell hooks (lib-codex-paths.sh, require-codex-readme-update.sh) and the shared Git invocation classifier that both commit-file-selection.py copies call. The guard engine uses its Python port, agent_guard.codex_payload.

hooks.name: lib-codex-paths.sh
hooks.note: Codex apply_patch/Edit/Write path extraction for the remaining shell hooks (load-elisp-after-edit.sh, regenerate-manual-after-edit.sh, remind-claude-readme-update.sh). The guard engine uses its Python port, agent_guard.codex_paths.

hooks.name: lib-python-heredoc.py
hooks.note: Classifier for quoted Python stdin heredocs. The guard engine loads the Claude copy (agent_guard.policies.secret_leak) and the Codex copy (Git projection in agent_guard.codex_payload, as lib-codex-hook-json.sh does). Unknown shapes stay conservative; not a sandbox.

hooks.name: lib-inert-mentions.py
hooks.note: Projection for agent_guard.policies.secret_leak: masks a protected tool name (pbpaste, pass, security) only as a plain argument of a read-only text tool, so searches and listings are not denied as credential reads; other positions stay fail-closed. The shared guard engine (lib/python/agent_guard, classifiers.py) loads this copy in-process for both runtimes; the Codex copy was removed at the 2026-10-01 cutover.

hooks.name: lib-repo-root.sh
hooks.note: Repo-root helper for the commit gates (require-doc-update.sh, require-readme-update.sh, require-codex-readme-update.sh). The Codex copy also asks lib-codex-hook-json.sh for an unambiguous parent functions.exec workdir. The guard engine's port is agent_guard.repo.

hooks.name: lib-staged-files.sh
hooks.note: Shared staged-file helper copied for commit gates; Codex usage comment references lib-codex-hook-json.sh.

hooks.name: commit-file-selection.py
hooks.note: Resolves proposed commit path selection using a disposable index, preserving unrelated staged changes.

hooks.name: load-elisp-after-edit.sh
hooks.note: Runtime-specific apply_patch/Edit/Write path adapters share the bounded manual export behavior. Both emit PostToolUse hookSpecificOutput with hookEventName and additionalContext, including sanitized partial-failure counts; a bare message field is invalid. Export failures use visible context with exit 0 because JSON accompanying a nonzero exit is ignored. No hook registration change is needed for the export-boundary repair.

hooks.name: notify-emacs-notification.sh
hooks.note: Claude Notification event; Codex routes Notification-equivalent events through codex-hook-wrapper directly.

hooks.name: notify-emacs-session-end.sh
hooks.note: Claude Stop event wrapper; Codex routes Stop through codex-hook-wrapper directly.

hooks.name: regenerate-manual-after-edit.sh
hooks.note: paired for apply_patch/Edit/Write path lists; both copies emit PostToolUse JSON per the shared hook contract: hookSpecificOutput must carry hookEventName and additionalContext (a bare message field fails Claude's schema validation and is dropped), and failure branches must exit 0 with decision/reason because JSON printed alongside a non-zero exit is ignored

hooks.name: regenerate-coverage-map.sh
hooks.note: Claude PostToolUse Edit|Write hook that refreshes rubric-visualizer coverage maps after CR task grading/rubric.md or grading/coverage-map.json edits. Codex has no matching global PostToolUse hook for this Trajectory-specific Claude workflow.

hooks.name: register-coverage-hook.py
hooks.note: One-shot helper used to register regenerate-coverage-map.sh in ~/.claude/settings.json; kept beside the runtime hook for local maintenance. It is not a runtime hook and has no Codex counterpart.

hooks.name: redact-secrets.sh
hooks.note: Bash output redaction filter. The guard engine's output wrapping (agent_guard.policies.dispatcher for Claude, codex_wrap for Codex) pipes credential-prone commands through this one copy for both runtimes.

hooks.name: remind-ai-config-sync.sh
hooks.note: paired as Claude/Codex wrappers around bin/ai-config-sync

hooks.name: remind-claude-readme-update.sh
hooks.note: paired for Codex apply_patch/Edit/Write path lists; both emit PostToolUse additionalContext JSON with hookEventName (plain Claude stdout never reached the model; fixed 2026-09-26). Codex side was re-indented and the in-dotfiles-repo short-circuit was lifted out of the per-path loop (cosmetic; Claude side was already correctly structured because it processes a single file_path).

hooks.name: require-codex-readme-update.sh
hooks.note: Codex README commit gate scoped to this dotfiles repository; the repo-root AGENTS.md project mirror is not treated as Codex integration. Runs for both agents from the global Git pre-commit hook through claude/bin/agent-commit-gates, which passes a canonical git commit so the staged files are read from the index.

hooks.name: require-doc-update.sh
hooks.note: Documentation commit gate. Runs for both agents from the global Git pre-commit hook through claude/bin/agent-commit-gates, which passes a canonical git commit so the staged files are read from the index.

hooks.name: require-readme-update.sh
hooks.note: Claude config README commit gate. Runs for both agents from the global Git pre-commit hook through claude/bin/agent-commit-gates, which passes a canonical git commit so the staged files are read from the index.

hooks.name: session-learning-capture.sh
hooks.note: Paired legacy Stop helper kept for tool parity, but it is not registered in live ~/.claude/settings.json or codex/hooks.json because Stop fires at turn end rather than true session exit. Session learning capture is prompted by the Emacs agent-before-exit path configured in emacs/config.org.

hooks.name: sync-reasoning-tasks-worktree.sh
hooks.note: Claude-only SessionStart support for reasoning-tasks worktrees, budgeted for its 30 s registration timeout (banner 15 s, fetch 10 s, merge aborted on TERM, atomic settings write; tests/test_sync_reasoning_tasks_hook.py runs the real hook). Key-link repair precedes eligibility guards; eligible worktrees sync upstream without pushing, reapply the local overlay, inject private project skills, and install freshness protection. The bulk wrapper fetches once. Codex has no SessionStart counterpart and uses creation-time Emacs setup or explicit shared sync. Full behavior: claude/hooks/README.org.

hooks.name: sync-agent-c-worktree.sh
hooks.note: Compatibility wrapper for the old SessionStart hook path after the conceptual-reasoning repo moved from agent-c to reasoning-tasks. It immediately execs claude/hooks/sync-reasoning-tasks-worktree.sh. No Codex counterpart for the same reason as the canonical hook: Codex has no matching SessionStart hook in this setup.

hooks.name: track-elisp-skill.sh
hooks.note: Depends on Claude Skill PostToolUse events; Codex has no matching Skill hook event in this setup.

hooks.name: cr-skill-routing-reminder.sh
hooks.note: Claude PreToolUse Edit/Write reminder: fires when editing a CR prompt/rubric/GOLDEN, telling the agent authoring is owned by /article-to-rubric (QA by /qa-reasoning) and to invoke the skill rather than hand-author. Non-blocking additionalContext. CR-scoped; no Codex peer.

hooks.name: cr-card-body-gate.sh
hooks.note: Claude PreToolUse Bash gate: denies a GitHub issue create/edit command when its --body-file is a CR card attempt that fails cr_card_body.py check (missing biblio/author/abstract), forcing CR cards through the template tool. Scoped to CR-card bodies; no Codex peer.

hooks.name: cr-issue-comment-freshness.sh
hooks.note: Claude-only PreToolUse gate registered in each reasoning-tasks worktree's untracked settings.local.json. It blocks issue-comment posting when a newer comment has not been acknowledged, includes the newest comment in the denial, and intentionally fails open on API errors. Codex posting is routed to Claude. Details live in claude/hooks/README.org.

hooks.name: lib-untrusted-execution.py
hooks.note: Static untrusted-execution classifier for agent_guard.policies.untrusted_execution; never executes the proposed command. Synthetic fixtures in tests/test_untrusted_execution_guard.py. The shared guard engine (lib/python/agent_guard, classifiers.py) loads this copy in-process for both runtimes; the Codex copy was removed at the 2026-10-01 cutover.

hooks.name: chrome-bridge-recover.py
hooks.note: Claude PostToolUse/PostToolUseFailure hook on mcp__claude-in-chrome__.*: when the bridge reports no connected browser, checks the native-messaging host chain and opens the Chrome profile mapped to this CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR in claude/chrome-extension-profiles.json, then tells the model to retry. No Codex counterpart: the Codex CLI drives Chrome through the playwright MCP server and the desktop app through its own plugin, not the Claude in Chrome extension.

hooks.name: redact-tool-output.py
hooks.note: Both mask tool output through redact-secrets.sh patterns and the known-value index (lib/python/secret_index.py), failing closed. Claude replaces the result via updatedToolOutput/updatedMCPToolOutput for every tool; Codex has no rewrite field, so it returns decision block with the masked output as the reason, for shell and MCP tools. Codex misses write_stdin chunks and error results.

hooks.name: agent-guard.sh
hooks.note: The only PreToolUse guard registration in both runtimes: runs lib/python/agent_guard (one policy module per former guard hook, chains in engine.py) and maps any status other than 0 to exit 2, so a missing interpreter, import error or crash denies. Intended differences from the shell guards: docs/plans/2026-10-01-guard-engine.md. Tests: bin/test-guards.

mcp_servers.note: Epoch's Asana MCP is project-local and must expose the same server to Claude Code and Codex with the Epoch Asana identity. The audit checks account identity via Asana /users/me and never compares or prints token values.

registrations.note: Tracked global Codex instruction counterpart. The live ~/.codex/AGENTS.md symlink points here because Codex does not apply project_doc_fallback_filenames to $CODEX_HOME.

Mutable live global settings; hook registrations are added in place. load-elisp-after-edit.sh is registered with timeout 150 (matching codex/hooks.json) because it waits up to 120 s for the Elpaca rebuild before reporting. Stop forwards turn-end state to Emacs, while session-learning capture belongs to the Emacs agent-before-exit path because Stop is not true process exit. Ahrefs, GitHub and Elisp Stop hook registration: claude/hooks/README.org. Since 2026-10-01 one PreToolUse registration, agent-guard.sh, runs every guard; chains in lib/python/agent_guard/engine.py.

Tracked source of the auto-mode classifier configuration (environment and allow entries, each list starting with $defaults). Installed by claude/bin/apply-auto-mode, which also offers --check for drift; run by the user, since the classifier's Self-Modification rule blocks a session from widening its own permissions. Claude-only: Codex has no auto-mode classifier.

Global registrations live through ~/.codex/hooks.json, outside repo-root .codex to avoid double loading. Lifecycle hooks use codex-hook-wrapper and an explicit Emacs socket. Shell matchers cover Bash, exec_command and functions.exec(_command); edit matchers are collapsed for trust review. Guards allow or deny, never ask. Since 2026-10-01 the shell and apply_patch|Edit|Write PreToolUse groups each run only agent-guard.sh (chains in lib/python/agent_guard/engine.py); its trust was renewed per home via the app-server API. New definitions need native trust. Output redactor 2026-09-30.

Shared deny-by-default allowlist for agent-initiated GitHub writes. Claude and Codex guards block git push and mutating gh operations unless the target repo matches an exact OWNER/REPO entry or OWNER/* account wildcard here. The benthamite/* entry permits repositories in Pablo's GitHub account; other entries should cover only repositories or accounts Pablo explicitly authorizes.

Codex model/trust/plugin/MCP/hook config. Account copies are writable and seeded by agent; retain .git/.agent-workspace project_root_markers in each. Claude loads ancestors natively (no config counterpart). Desktop owns per-home browser hashes; the shim retains signed runtimes. CODEX_CLI_PATH: Resources/codex-cli/bin/codex. Preserve hook source/key/hash trust; new hooks need hooks/list and config/batchWrite per home. skill-prune disables skills; codex-config-prune removes dead records. Moves require trust-key rewrites; Trajectory trust is retired. See codex/README.org.

Ensures the live ~/.codex/skills directory is a symlink to the tracked codex/skills tree because Codex discovers global skills from ~/.codex/skills/*/SKILL.md. Also installs local gitignored private-skill shims from the encrypted private manifest.

Creates local gitignored private-skill shims under the live skill roots from ai-config-sync.private.json, so explicit private $skill invocations resolve without tracking private names or bodies in the public repo.

Codex-only command allowlist rules, pruned 2026-07-29 to generic recurring commands only (git add/commit/push/restore, curl -L, ps, emacs batch, emacsclient --eval). One-off approvals, dead-PID kills, the AGENTS.md symlink rule, and the arbitrary-command CODEX_HOME env prefix were removed; do not re-add task-specific or PID-specific rules. There is no Claude counterpart; material policy changes should be recorded here.

Reads Google Drive's native sync-error panel through the accessibility API — the only way to reach it, since Drive exposes no file or API — and marks each reported name stale or live by resolving it against the Drive tree. Drive's list does not clear itself when the offending path disappears, so the raw count overstates the problem badly; the 2026-08-03 panel showed 200+ errors against 8 live offenders. Owned by the fix-drive-errors skill.
